supporting_observations.claim: The domain controller recorded two failed network logons for tom.weber from the same reported source address, 203.0.113.17. Both used NTLM and had a bad-password substatus.
About 84 seconds after the second failure, the domain controller recorded a successful network Kerberos logon for tom.weber from that same reported source address.

The failure-then-success sequence from a source not identified in the supplied inventory as an authorized remote-administration host supports treating the alerted activity as potentially unauthorized; the records do not establish who controlled that source.

known_telemetry_limitations: Proxy log collection was unavailable from 13:25 to 14:10 UTC on the proxy, covering the alerted authentication events. This limitation is from the supplied sensor-coverage status; no proxy records are available for that interval.

The reported source address is 203.0.113.17. The evidence does not explain whether this address is literal or a sanitized placeholder, so its real-world attribution cannot be verified from these logs.
claims_not_established: Whether the successful logon was performed by tom.weber or an unauthorized party.
Whether the reported source address maps to a specific external host, intermediary, or sanitized address.
What activity, if any, followed the successful network logon.
additional_evidence_needed: Validate the source address against network, firewall, NAT, and authentication infrastructure records, including whether the address was sanitized.
Correlate the successful logon with endpoint or network telemetry identifying the originating system and any resulting access.
Confirm with tom.weber whether the authentication was expected and review account and credential-change activity around the event.
